recommendation: Keep this no-change audit as-is for FHIR-39243. Any cleanup of ignored historical XML comments or generated-looking diagrams should be handled separately because the authoritative current source already implements the required relocation.
issue_request: FHIR-39243 was a Published/Persuasive OO change request, applied for R5, asking to move patient association out of Device and explicitly resolving by linking to FHIR-38904. The concern was that Device.association[0..*].humanSubject could retain multiple patients' identifying information in Device and leak PHI through patient-compartment access.
initial_application: No source commit was found that mentions FHIR-39243 directly. The linked FHIR-38904 implementation path added DeviceAssociation in 620b8fa10c, commented out Device.association and Device subject/patient search parameters in 97e59d026d, and QA-adjusted DeviceAssociation in 7a135eb348.
additional_context: FHIR-38637 and FHIR-39009 were also resolved by the FHIR-38904 disposition, and FHIR-39226 is a companion ballot issue with the same request. Current fhir.ini keeps Device and DeviceAssociation active, classifies Device as business and DeviceAssociation as patient, and maps Device.patient to DeviceAssociation; community planning records group the same issue family.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. Comment-stripped checks of Device structure/search-parameter source found no active Device.association, humanSubject, Device-subject, or Device-patient definitions; DeviceAssociation active source contains subject/period and patient/subject search parameters, and Device narrative directs ownership/custodianship relationships to DeviceAssociation.

related_jiras.note: Controlling linked disposition that created DeviceAssociation and removed the active Device patient association.
Period-on-Device.association request was overcome by DeviceAssociation under FHIR-38904.
Device subject reference conflict was linked to the same FHIR-38904 disposition.
Companion ballot issue with the same request and the same FHIR-38904-linked resolution.
